folds.heading: ## Content reconciliation B292: Lin author tooling and diagnostic scope
folds.body:
The full [Lin tooling audition](gm/dispatch/foundation-completion-2026-10-12/research/TOOLING_AUDITION.md) retains useful T1–T5/A1–A4 findings without selecting a new authoring stack. Its installed compiler exactly reproduced the then-current 124,528-byte artifact with zero diagnostics; the unknown-response trial exposed a generic error while syntax/missing-divert already had a file/line. A narrow real edit can justify scene/response context, preserving stable IDs, unique choice tags, observer-safe fields and admission allowlists. This is observed diagnostic friction, not measured faster authoring or proof of native Lin consent/stock/transaction behavior.

The project-local INCLUDE rejection and pin/format checks govern that historical recipe. An editor supporting includes does not change admission. The local inkjs2.4.0 pin and older upstream compatibility-table endpoint are distinct evidence, not a new version upgrade task. Inky was an unrun optional editor trial and one absent Applications path did not prove global absence. Yarn/Twine documentation supplied design comparisons, not a browser bridge, persisted-cursor migration or selected license-qualified dependency. The same-scene author-time/host-edit/branch-visibility audition was future work. Reuse native consequence and current-format cursor/persistence authority instead of a second dialogue writer. Exact compiler/runtime notices and upstream attribution remain with their owner; no install, external source copy, compiler rerun or author-productivity claim is made by this fold.

folds.heading: ## Content reconciliation B292: benchmark reproduction and kernel durability limits
folds.body:
The full [ER7 reproduction README](gm/dispatch/engine-runtime-2026-10-14/ER7/README.md) and [ER14 spike README](gm/dispatch/engine-runtime-2026-10-14/ER14/spike/README.md) are archived experiment evidence. Their shell/install/benchmark instructions are not requests to execute again. ER7 runs isolated Node actors/workers/save microbenchmarks without repository imports, not browser durability or gameplay. A changed host/runtime or present performance question needs its own measured relevant input, not a new timestamp on old instructions.

ER14 has one synthetic advance owner, declared dependency/event/sequence ordering and per-operation rollback on trusted fixture functions. It is not a sandbox or arbitrary production plugin host. Command idempotency is distinct from unique job slots. Most importantly, command success and explicit storage are separate: failed save may leave live state newer than the stored snapshot. Filesystem temporary rename without fsync and memory-manifest failure preservation do not establish the production durable-save-before-publication contract or browser storage atomicity. Loading validates referenced chunks before publication, while declared reverse dependencies cannot detect omitted declarations. Incremental-save byte reporting still reads all referenced chunks.

Exact split/replay evidence is local to fixed fixture/content/seeds/commands and the stated default-off hunger/weather/home-world context. The enabled-hunger floating-point counterexample remains a counterexample rather than being hidden by the narrow pass. Native pause/choice/life barriers, changing world/season context, stock-backed meals, calendar publication, browser writer authority/import, bounded receipt/replay/GC and migrations/future-field preservation were explicitly omitted. No benchmark, dependency, source copy, browser, kernel migration, save format or production replacement is selected by this review. Preserve the experiments as references for an actual chosen consumer, with their measured and omitted contracts separate.
